newsitem.title: USA: More pregnant American women drinking alcohol.
newsitem.headline: More pregnant American women drinking alcohol.

text.p: More American women are drinking alcohol during pregnancy, increasing the chance that their babies will suffer from birth defects and mental retardation, federal health officials said on Thursday.

The Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said 3.5 percent of pregnant women surveyed were frequent drinkers, averaging more than one drink a day or having a minimum of five drinks on at least one occasion during the preceding month.

The rate of frequent drinking in the latest survey was more than four times higher than 1991, when 0.8 percent of pregnant women said they were frequent drinkers. The CDC estimated at least 140,000 pregnant women were drinking at such levels every year.

The agency said consuming alcohol during pregnancy caused Foetal Alcohol Syndrome, a leading cause of birth defects and mental retardation. Since 1981, the government has warned pregnant women, and those planning to become pregnant, not to drink.
"This is a dangerous and risky behaviour and can have serious lifelong consequences on their unborn child," CDC statistician Beth Luman said.

The latest survey, conducted in 1995, found that 16.3 percent of pregnant women surveyed said they had had at least one alcoholic drink in the past month. The 1991 survey found that 12.4 percent of pregnant women had drunk alcohol.

Researchers said their survey of more than 33,000 women aged 18 to 44 found no comparable increases in drinking or frequent drinking among women who were not pregnant. The CDC said women who might become pregnant should be aware of the risks.
"Because over half of the pregnancies in the United States are unintentional or unplanned, many women don't know that they're pregnant until well into their first trimester," Luman said.
Foetal Alcohol Syndrome is characterised by facial abnormalities, growth retardation and central nervous system deficits including learning and developmental disorders, the CDC said.
